Chapter 8: The Neurology of Free Will—How Much Control Do We Really Have?
When we start looking closely at our habits, it’s natural to wonder—if so much of what we do is automatic, how much control do we actually have?
The answer really comes down to how our brains balance automatic routines with conscious choice.
Think about it: the brain’s habit system is all about efficiency. Once we turn a behavior into a habit, it barely takes any mental effort. That frees up our attention for other things, which is handy, but it also means we might go through the motions without even realizing it.
So, does that mean we’re just passengers along for the ride? Not quite. Here’s where it gets interesting—awareness is the game-changer.
When you start to notice the cues and rewards that drive your routines, you create a tiny space for choice to step in.
Research has found there’s this pivotal moment—right before a habit kicks in—when you can actually choose to do something different.
Picture this: you’re in a meeting, and you feel that familiar urge to check your phone. That’s your cue. But if you pause, even for just a second, you open up a window to make a new choice.
Maybe, instead of reaching for your device, you take a deep breath, or jot down a quick note about what triggered the urge. Over time, these small, conscious actions can start to rewire your habit loop.
So, how can you actually put this into practice?
Here are some practical ways to exercise your free will when it comes to habits:
First, boost your self-awareness. Pay attention to the moments when cravings or urges pop up.
Next, build in pause points. Give yourself a brief moment to reflect before jumping into automatic action.
Practice mindfulness—techniques like deep breathing or grounding can help you stay present and notice what’s happening in real time.
And finally, have a plan for what to do instead. Preparing an alternative routine makes it much easier to switch gears when you catch yourself in the old pattern.
Here’s the heart of it: habits are powerful, but they don’t define you. The ability to choose—even in those tiny moments—is what gives you agency.
By growing your awareness and making intentional choices, you can take back control over your routines and really shape the life you want.
